title: eval-harness: add prompt-regression CI hook with heuristic thresholds and report summary
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary: Add a GitHub Actions + lightweight Python CI hook that runs the eval-harness prompt-set regression check for changed prompt sets and publishes a compact result summary to the PR. Motivation: we observed a few incident post-deploy regressions that originated from prompt changes and lack of early feedback on prompt-level quality impact. This hook is intended to catch high-confidence regressions in token-level and embedding-sim metrics before merge.

What this PR does: - Introduces .github/workflows/eval-prompt-regression.yml that triggers on PRs when files under eval/prompt-sets/ change. - Implements scripts/ci/prompt_regression_hook.py which executes a sampled eval run (configurable subset + seeds), computes metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-L, embedding cosine sim via existing embed pipeline), aggregates per-prompt deltas, and applies an adaptive heuristic threshold (default: >1.5% absolute drop for quality metrics OR >0.03 drop in mean embedding-sim for top-k responses) to surface likely regressions. - Adds eval-harness/hooks/regression.py to centralize comparison logic and a small public API used by both the CLI harness and the CI hook. - Adds tests/tests_eval/test_prompt_regression_hook.py and minimal docs/docs/ops/prompt-regression-ci.md. - The hook posts a check-run summary and a comment with top-5 regressions (prompt id, metric, delta, example diff), and fails the check if the number of flagged prompts exceeds the configured NOR threshold (default 1).

Design notes: - The thresholds are configurable via repo .eval-config.yml; the PR includes sane defaults tuned against historical prompt changes (see linked Linear ticket ENG-2024). - To limit cost, CI runs a sampled evaluation (default 200 examples or the full changed prompt set, whichever is smaller); sampling is deterministic per PR to make reruns comparable. - False positives are expected; the summary includes a "mark as expected" quick link (requires maintainers) which records an exemption in .eval-exemptions.json.

Checklist: - [x] Add GitHub Action workflow - [x] Implement hook script and harness integration - [x] Unit tests for comparison logic - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Config defaults and example exemptions file

Commit summary: - Add eval prompt regression hook workflow (main action) - Add prompt_regression_hook.py and integrate with eval-harness - Add unit tests and fixtures - Docs: ops runbook and configuration guide

Files changed (high level): - .github/workflows/eval-prompt-regression.yml: new workflow that installs python deps, runs the hook for changed prompt sets, uploads annotated summary artifacts. - scripts/ci/prompt_regression_hook.py: entrypoint for CI (200 lines, uses eval-harness internal API). - eval-harness/hooks/regression.py: comparison utilities and metric converters. - tests/tests_eval/test_prompt_regression_hook.py: pytest cases for regression detection and exemption logic. - docs/docs/ops/prompt-regression-ci.md: runbook and troubleshooting.

Testing: - Local unit tests: all pass. - End-to-end on staging: ran against a known regression dataset (from ENG-2024) to validate flags; produced 3 flagged prompts (expected). - GitHub Actions: first run failed due to missing small packaging issue; fixed in second commit and final run passed.

Follow-ups / future work: - Add richer quality signals (semantic eval, human-in-the-loop flagging) - Surface per-model and per-deployment rollout risk scores in the Console - Add a non-blocking `warning` mode and a historical regression dashboard
commits: c1a3b5f: add workflow and initial hook implementation
d4e6f7a: fix packaging in CI environment (install eval-harness as package)
e8f9a0b: tests and docs for prompt-regression hook
review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Nice end-to-end. Can we make the threshold value configurable via org default as well as repo config? I can see teams wanting different sensitivity.
Aisha Patel: Agree; added .eval-config.yml with repo defaults and a note in docs about org-level overrides. The hook reads REPO_CONFIG first, then org config via environment variables if present.
Evelyn Chen: Tests look good. One nit: the CI comment contains raw examples that may include PII — please ensure the redaction util is used.
Aisha Patel: Good catch. Hook now pipes examples through redact_for_ci() (uses existing redaction util in eval-harness).
Devon Mills: Approving pending the small packaging fix in the second commit — verified the final CI run passes.
release_notes: Add prompt-regression CI hook: runs eval-harness on prompt-set changes and blocks merge on high-confidence regressions. Configurable via .eval-config.yml.
